topics.label: Lecture introduction: overview of inflammation initiation and resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and pedagogical goals for the lecture.

topics.label: Principles of innate sensing via PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system distinguishes self from non-self by detecting conserved molecular patterns and signs of cellular damage through strategically located receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families, signalling pathways, and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific receptor systems, including Toll-like receptors, cytoplasmic sensors, and the inflammasome, and how their intracellular signalling drives inflammatory cytokine activation.

topics.label: Inflammatory response execution, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the physiological progression of acute inflammation, including sentinel cell mediator release, leukocyte recruitment, lymphatic priming, and severe systemic manifestations like sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic persistence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is brought to an end, the cellular mechanisms restoring tissue integrity, and the structural adaptations that arise when inflammation cannot be fully resolved.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion: transition to complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
